item.title: Reverse-a-function drill — 2026-10-28
item.description:
Reverse-a-function drill — 2026-10-28
Target: Windows x86-64 (arg in `ecx`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: lea eax, [rcx-48] cmp eax, 9 setbe al movzx eax, al ret ```
There is only one comparison and no `&&`. What does it compute, and why does it work?
## Answer
```c int mystery(int c) { return c >= '0' && c <= '9'; // isdigit for ASCII } ```
## Explanation
- `lea eax,[rcx-48]` is just a subtract (48 = `'0'`) that leaves flags alone; `c` in `'0'..'9'` becomes 0..9. - `setbe` is an *unsigned* test (CF=1 or ZF=1): any `c < 48` wraps to a huge unsigned value (e.g. 47 → 0xFFFFFFFF), so it fails `<= 9` too. - One unsigned compare thus checks both bounds: `(unsigned)(c - lo) <= (hi - lo)` is the standard compiler range-check trick.
